title: Control Scripts and Results
intro: The control language turns ngspice from a program that runs one analysis into one that runs experiments: loops over values and corners, measurements, statistics and files for other tools. This chapter covers it, and how to fix simulations that do not converge.

items: The Control Language: vectors, variables, plots, expressions, control structures, and the commands that change and rerun a circuit.
Measurements: every form of .meas and meas: delays, crossings, averages, integrals, derivatives and expressions.
Output, Plotting and Data Files: save, print, wrdata, rawfiles, gnuplot, pyplot and hardcopy, and reading results in Python.
Sweeps, Corners and Monte Carlo: parameter and temperature sweeps, process corners from library sections, and Monte Carlo with statistics.
Convergence and Accuracy: what the error messages mean, the options that matter, and a checklist for circuits that will not simulate.
